messages:
kevin: hey team, kevin here — first day. i'm trying to run the runtime in a dev container on WSL2/Docker Desktop and unit tests immediately segfault during GPU init. any tips?

kevin: i built inside container from source using our Dockerfile (based on nvidia/cuda:12.2.0-devel-ubuntu22.04) and ran tests with `pytest tests/gpu`. tests crash with a SIGSEGV in cudnn convolution init.

sara: welcome! :wave: segfault in cuDNN often means the container sees a different driver/devlib on the host than the libcudnn in the image expects. can you run `docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:12.2.0-base-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi` on your machine? and `docker exec -it <cid> bash -c 'ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudnn.so | head'` inside the failing container?

kevin: `docker run ... nvidia-smi` returns Driver Version: 535.86.05, CUDA Version: 12.2. inside my runtime container `ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudnn.so.8` shows it links to `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcublas.so.12` and libcudnn2 -> not found.

mohit: seems like your image has libcudnn installed in /usr/local/cuda but the runtime resolves to host-installed libs in /usr/lib via the container's ld paths. on WSL/Docker Desktop we sometimes hit mixed mounts where host lib dirs shadow image libs. what base image are you using for the test container (devel vs base)?

kevin: our build image is `runtime-dev:local` which installs cudnn via apt from Ubuntu repos (leftover from a dev experiment). base image was devel.

sara: two problems: 1) mixing host libs and image libs; 2) apt-installed cudnn can be an ABI mismatch. recommended: use the official CUDA container with matching cudnn (nvidia/cuda:12.2.0-cudnn8-devel-ubuntu22.04) or in your Dockerfile add the NVIDIA cudnn deb repository and install cudnn8 that matches the driver. Also ensure you run with `--gpus all` and that the container runtime is set to `nvidia` (Docker Desktop settings) or that you have the NVIDIA Container Toolkit installed on WSL.

mohit: on WSL you also need to check Docker Desktop's GPU support toggle and that your WSL distro's kernel supports GPU passthrough. run `wsl --status` on the host and confirm WSLg + GPU support. we've seen people with old WSL kernels where containers crash with cuDNN segfaults.

kevin: i checked `wsl --status` — WSL version 0.67, Kernel: 5.15.90. Docker Desktop GPU toggle is on. i switched my Dockerfile to use `nvidia/cuda:12.2.0-cudnn8-devel-ubuntu22.04` and rebuilt the image. still segfaults.

sara: inside the rebuilt container, run `python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available()); print(torch.version.cuda)"` if you have pytorch, or run a minimal cuda sample to call cuDNN init. Also check `ldd $(python -c "import torch; print(torch._C.__file__)")` to see what libraries PyTorch is binding to.

kevin: minimal repro: a tiny C++ program calling cudnnCreate(&h) segfaults at load time. `strace` shows the container's loader opening `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudnn.so.8` which doesn't exist, then fallback to `/usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudnn.so.8` and then calls into libcublas in /usr/lib which causes mismatch.

mohit: sounds like an ldconfig/ld.so.conf issue inside container. run `ldconfig -p | grep cudnn` and check `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/*` inside the container. Make sure `/usr/local/cuda/lib64` is earlier in ld.so paths. You can also set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in your test command as a quick workaround. Long-term: ensure the image has a consistent set of nvidia libs and avoid installing distro cuda packages that conflict.

sara: one more gotcha on Windows hosts: Docker Desktop sometimes mounts host `/usr/lib` into the container for WSL interoperability; check `docker inspect <cid>` Mounts. If you see a mount mapping host `/usr/lib` into the container, that's the culprit. Uncheck any file sharing options that mount host lib dirs, or prefer building/running in a dedicated Linux VM rather than WSL until tooling stabilizes.

kevin: found mount mapping `/usr/lib` from host into container — that was the cause. disabled that in Docker Desktop file sharing, rebuilt `runtime-dev:local` using the cudnn-enabled base image, set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in the test runner, and tests now run without segfault. :tada:

infra-bot: build infra note: prefer official `nvidia/cuda:<version>-cudnn8-*` images for local dev; avoid mixing distro cuda packages with runfile images.

onboard-bot: Welcome kevin! Please complete the "Runtime dev setup" checklist in Notion and paste your working image tag in the onboarding doc.

kevin: thanks all, will file a tiny PR to the README describing WSL/Docker Desktop mount pitfalls and our recommended base image.
_description: Onboarding thread: new hire debugging cuDNN SIGSEGV inside Docker on WSL2 due to host '/usr/lib' being mounted into container and mixed libcudnn/libcublas versions; team recommends using official cudnn base image, checking mounts, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, and WSL settings.
